title: What training do the CMS hospital Conditions of Participation require?
description: Training duties in the CMS hospital Conditions of Participation, 42 CFR 482: emergency preparedness, restraint, infection control and more, at November 2026.
shortAnswer: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) hospital Conditions of Participation in 42 CFR Part 482 contain several separate staff training duties. The main ones are emergency preparedness training at hire and at least every 2 years (482.15(d)), restraint and seclusion competency before use and at orientation (482.13(f)), competency-based infection control training (482.42), and annual training on emergency readiness and transfer protocols. A maternal care training standard takes effect January 1, 2027.
keyTakeaways: There is no single training clause in 42 CFR 482. Training duties are spread across individual Conditions of Participation, each with its own audience, trigger and record.

Emergency preparedness at 482.15(d) requires initial training for all new and existing staff, contractors and volunteers, training at least every 2 years, demonstrated knowledge, and retraining after significant policy updates.

Restraint and seclusion training at 482.13(f) must be completed, with demonstrated competency, before staff apply restraints, at orientation, and periodically after that, and be recorded in personnel files.
Since July 1, 2025, hospitals must train relevant staff annually on emergency services readiness protocols (482.55(c)) and on patient transfer policies (482.43(c)).
From January 1, 2027, hospitals with obstetrical services must give relevant staff initial and then biennial maternal care training under 482.59(c).
regulator: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), US Department of Health and Human Services
appliesTo: Hospitals participating in Medicare and Medicaid, including hospitals accredited by a CMS-approved accrediting organization for deemed status
Hospital staff, medical staff, individuals providing services under arrangement, contracted personnel and volunteers, as each standard specifies
Psychiatric hospitals, which must also meet 42 CFR 482.1 through 482.23 and 482.25 through 482.57

sections.heading: How do the hospital Conditions of Participation set training requirements?

blocks.text: The hospital Conditions of Participation (CoPs) set training duties topic by topic rather than in one workforce training clause. Each CoP in 42 CFR Part 482 is a condition a hospital must meet to take part in Medicare and Medicaid, and several contain a standard that names who must be trained, when, and what must be documented. Surveyors from state survey agencies or accrediting organizations check these during surveys.

The practical result is that a hospital needs a register of CoP training obligations, each mapped to the roles it covers. A [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) built from that register is the usual way to show surveyors that every in-scope role has the right training at the right interval. The requirements below are stated as at November 2026 and were read in the version of 42 CFR 482 that eCFR showed as current to November 5, 2026.

sections.heading: What emergency preparedness training does 482.15(d) require?

blocks.text: Hospitals must run an emergency preparedness training and testing program based on their emergency plan, risk assessment, policies and communication plan, and must review and update it at least every 2 years. The training program in [42 CFR 482.15(d)(1)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-G/part-482/subpart-B/section-482.15) has five elements.

items: Initial training in emergency preparedness policies and procedures for all new and existing staff, individuals providing services under arrangement, and volunteers, consistent with their expected role.
Emergency preparedness training at least every 2 years.
Demonstration of staff knowledge of emergency procedures.
Training on updated policies and procedures if they are significantly updated.

blocks.text: Testing is separate from training. Under 482.15(d)(2) the hospital must conduct exercises to test the emergency plan at least twice per year, including an annual full-scale community-based exercise or, when that is not accessible, an annual individual facility-based functional exercise. A hospital that activates its plan for an actual emergency is exempt from its next required full-scale or functional exercise. Exercise participation can feed the demonstration of staff knowledge, but it does not replace the training record.

sections.heading: What restraint and seclusion training must staff complete?

blocks.text: Staff who apply restraints, implement seclusion, or monitor, assess or care for a restrained or secluded patient must be trained and able to demonstrate competency before doing so, as part of orientation, and periodically after that, consistent with hospital policy. This is the Patient's Rights standard at [42 CFR 482.13(f)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-G/part-482/subpart-B/section-482.13).

The required content is specific. It covers techniques to identify behaviors and triggers, nonphysical intervention skills, choosing the least restrictive intervention, safe application of all restraint types used in the hospital (including recognizing signs of distress such as positional asphyxia), recognizing when restraint is no longer needed, monitoring physical and psychological well-being, and first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation certification with periodic recertification. Trainers must be qualified by education, training and experience, and the hospital must record successful completion and demonstrated competency in staff personnel records.

Physicians and other licensed practitioners who order restraint must, at a minimum, have a working knowledge of hospital restraint policy (482.13(e)(11)). A registered nurse who performs the one-hour face-to-face evaluation must have completed the 482.13(f) training.

sections.heading: What infection control and antibiotic stewardship training is required?

blocks.text: Hospitals must provide competency-based training and education on the practical application of infection prevention and control, and of antibiotic stewardship, to hospital personnel and staff, including medical staff and, as applicable, contracted personnel. Under [42 CFR 482.42(c)(2)(iv)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-G/part-482/subpart-C/section-482.42), the infection preventionist is responsible for the infection control training; under 482.42(c)(3)(iv), the antibiotic stewardship leader is responsible for the stewardship training.

The rule does not set a frequency. It says "competency-based", which points to assessed performance rather than attendance alone, and it ties the training to the hospital's own guidelines, policies and procedures. Hospitals with staff exposed to blood also have to meet the separate annual OSHA requirement; see [OSHA bloodborne pathogens training](/regulations/osha-bloodborne-pathogens-training-requirements).

sections.heading: Which annual training requirements took effect in 2025?

blocks.text: Two annual training standards took effect on July 1, 2025, both added by a CMS final rule published November 27, 2024. Under the emergency services readiness standard at [42 CFR 482.55(c)(3)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-G/part-482/subpart-D/section-482.55), applicable staff, as identified by the hospital, must be trained annually on the emergency readiness protocols and provisions, including protocols for obstetrical emergencies.

For that standard, the governing body must identify and document which staff must complete the training, the hospital must record completion in staff personnel records, it must be able to demonstrate staff knowledge, and it must use findings from its quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI) program to update training topics. Separately, the transfer protocols standard at [42 CFR 482.43(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-G/part-482/subpart-C/section-482.43) requires annual training for relevant staff on the hospital's policies and procedures for transferring patients to the appropriate level of care.

sections.heading: What maternal care training starts in 2027?

blocks.text: From January 1, 2027, hospitals that offer obstetrical services must ensure relevant staff are trained on facility-identified evidence-based best practices and protocols to improve maternal care. The standard is at [42 CFR 482.59(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-G/part-482/subpart-D/section-482.59).

blocks.title: Not yet in effect as at November 2026
blocks.text: The obstetrical services staff training standard at 482.59(c) is effective January 1, 2027. It requires initial training for relevant new staff, governing body identification of staff who must complete initial and subsequent biennial training, documentation in personnel records, demonstrated staff knowledge, and use of QAPI findings to update topics.

Hospitals have about seven weeks from the date of this page to identify the in-scope roles and schedule initial training. For practical steps when a requirement changes, see [how to update training when regulations change](/guides/how-to-update-training-when-regulations-change).

sections.heading: How can a hospital map CoP training duties to roles and evidence?

blocks.text: Map each standard to the roles it covers, the interval, and the record a surveyor will ask for. The table below is a starting register built from the CoP text. It is not exhaustive, and service-specific CoPs (for example nuclear medicine or psychiatric hospitals) add their own personnel requirements.

Many hospitals are also accredited, and accreditation standards add competence expectations of their own; see [Joint Commission staff competency expectations](/regulations/joint-commission-staff-competency-requirements).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry represents each CoP standard as an obligation linked to the roles it names, the hospital policies it depends on, and the assessment points that show demonstrated knowledge. When a policy such as the emergency plan is significantly updated, the affected roles can be identified and assigned retraining from those links. See how this works for [healthcare and life sciences organizations](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Do volunteers need emergency preparedness training?
faqs.a: Yes. 42 CFR 482.15(d)(1)(i) requires initial emergency preparedness training for all new and existing staff, individuals providing services under arrangement, and volunteers, consistent with their expected roles. Training then recurs at least every 2 years and after significant updates to the policies and procedures.

faqs.q: Does the hospital CoP require annual training for all staff?
faqs.a: No single CoP requires annual training for all staff. Annual intervals apply to specific topics, such as emergency services readiness and transfer protocols since July 1, 2025. Emergency preparedness is at least every 2 years, restraint training is periodic per hospital policy, and infection control training has no set interval. Many hospitals choose annual cycles for simplicity.

faqs.q: Who decides which staff need emergency readiness training?
faqs.a: The hospital does. Under 482.55(c)(3), applicable staff are identified by the hospital, and the governing body must identify and document which staff must complete the training. Surveyors can be expected to compare that documented list with personnel file completion records.

faqs.q: Does accreditation replace the CoP training requirements?
faqs.a: No. Accreditation is a route to showing compliance, not a substitute for the CoPs, which still apply. Joint Commission, for example, describes its hospital standards as building on the CoPs and identifies CoP-based requirements separately from its own National Performance Goals, which add expectations such as training and evaluation of staff competence.
